- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–3% of recent mean.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 1–2 day lag correction by reducing forecast by 1–2% per day post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates near-term (first 7–10 days) and underestimates long-term (last 15–20 days); adjust with sentiment-weighted smoothing: higher sentiment → more aggressive short-term correction.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2 → 0.8), model tends to misalign with sentiment cycles; apply a 1–2 day smoothing filter to forecast to reduce volatility mismatch.
